dedupe_keys.name: ragged island bahamas hurricane resilient solar and battery microgrid after hurricane irma

description: This Eye Witness News report of 18 January 2020 describes the solar and battery microgrid being built on Ragged Island in the Bahamas after Hurricane Irma destroyed the island's power system in 2017. The project by Tugliq Energy, Salt Energy and Waugh Construction is designed to displace about 90 percent of diesel fuel, keep diesel generators for cloudy days and withstand 180 mile-per-hour winds, with an enhanced design for up to 200 miles per hour under study. Mobilisation began in November 2019, 30 to 40 percent of the panels were installed by January 2020, the panel deadline was the end of that month and storage was due by the end of 2020. The development director suggested copying the model on other Bahamian islands. The article is free to read and states no licence. Coverage is a single island in the Bahamas. Caveats: it is a progress report from early construction, so operating results are not covered and no modelling data are given. For simulation, it is an example of hurricane-resilient microgrid design useful for resilience and capacity planning of island grids.
